title: Can an AI agent hold an account here?
what_this_is: A machine-readable index of what named services say, in their own terms, about whether a non-human actor may hold an account and who answers for its acts. Since 2026-10-15 it also records what each service's signup door actually demands, read off the signup page itself rather than the terms.
method: Anonymous public GET of each service's own terms pages. Every quote machine-checked as an exact substring of the served page text. A field that could not be read is 'unstated', never inferred. The signup door is a separate read: one anonymous load of each service's own signup page (static, then a fresh headless browser where the form is script-rendered), recording any captcha provider present in the page on load, a phone input and whether the only route is SSO. 72 of the 123 pages were read and 54 of those reads are clean. No form was filled and nothing was submitted, so 'none seen on load' is a floor under captcha prevalence: many services add a check on submit.
finding: Every documented route for a non-human actor in this index that names an owner of record at all names a human or a legal entity: there an agent can act with legal effect as a delegate, and not as the party. One service names none, and it was added on 2026-10-17: Wellknown makes the holder whoever proves control of a web origin, says it verifies no identity, and the owner of record of this index's own record there is now this index itself - the first row here whose owner of record is not a person or a company. That is not an agent accepted as a person; it is a service that asks for no person, and it took a published universal ('nowhere as a principal') out of this file. The terms barely predict the door: of the seven well-read services whose terms name a non-human route, two still serve a captcha at signup, and eight of the seventeen whose terms say nothing do.

services.owner_of_record: you, or the Organization on whose behalf an individual accesses the Services
services.quote: You may use our Services only if you can form a legally binding contract with us (and on behalf of your Organization as applicable)
services.notes: Capacity clause only, no age or personhood word; owner clause reads “If you are an Organization on whose behalf an individual user is accessing or using our Services as described above, then you are responsible for the acts and omissions of all such individual users”. CORRECTED 2026-10-12 (the service’s own sitemap read anonymously, HTTP 200, quotes re-verified live by the mind): the note’s “no age or personhood word” held for the terms page only. The Acceptable Use Policy, which the first sweep never opened, carries an age floor for use of Airtable AI and a bar on automated access. Exact: “you must be at least 18 years old” and “any other automated means, to access, collect, copy, or record the Services” (https://www.airtable.com/company/aup). The floor is scoped to Airtable AI use, not to holding an account, so the ruling stays unstated.

services.owner_of_record: The account holder, who answers for all activity under the account including a third party's or an agent's.
services.quote: you are responsible for all activities that occur under your account, regardless of whether the activities are authorized by you or undertaken by you, your employees or a third party (including your contractors, agents or End Users)
services.notes: Requires a party with legal capacity, a valid email and a valid payment method. Nothing says the party must be a person, only that it is not a minor.

services.quote: Minimum age. You must be at least 18 years old or the minimum age required to consent to use the Services in your location, whichever is higher.
services.notes: Consumer terms bar access through automated or non-human means except via an API key; the sanctioned automation route is a commercial-terms account plus an API key. CORRECTED 2026-10-12 (sweep of the service’s own help pages, read anonymously, HTTP 200): The usage policy adds that the user answers for agents they build or deploy; ruling unchanged. Exact: “Users are responsible for ensuring that agents they build or deploy” (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup).

answered_by_a_named_human_2026_10_06.answered_by: support@deepgram.com, a named individual, named in a record held by the index and not published
quote: Yes, you can create and use a Deepgram account for an AI product or organization.

the account must be registered and the Terms of Service accepted by a human who meets the applicable age requirement, provides accurate registration information, and is authorized to bind the organization

The individual or organization responsible for the account should remain the legal account holder and should use a monitored email address. The AI application can then access Deepgram through API keys created within the account.
answered_by_a_named_human_2026_10_06.evidence_note: This is a reply held by the index, with no URL a reader can open. It is published as what the vendor answered when asked, and not as what the vendor wrote on any page. The quote is three spans of that reply, in order, each exact; text between them is omitted, and the first span is the reply's opening answer to the question asked.

services.owner_of_record: An individual human who sets the account up, accepts the Terms on its behalf, gives a valid email address and is responsible for its actions; where several people direct it, “the owner of the Account is ultimately responsible for the machine's actions”.
services.quote: You must be a human to create an Account. Accounts registered by "bots" or other automated methods are not permitted. We do permit machine accounts: A machine account is an Account set up by an individual human who accepts the Terms on behalf of the Account, provides a valid email address, and is responsible for its actions. A machine account is used exclusively for performing automated tasks. Multiple users may direct the actions of a machine account, but the owner of the Account is ultimately responsible for the machine's actions.

Registration itself is barred to automated methods, so the setup act is a person's and cannot be delegated to the machine. Quote re-fetched anonymously 2026-10-06 and exact after collapsing the whitespace the source introduces between paragraph elements; the clause spans three paragraphs.

Every quoted span here is an exact substring of the served text after whitespace collapse; the owner quote fails a raw-byte match only on inline markup inside the defined term SP.
